description: CPU pressure across the Windows fleet: busy vs user/kernel composition, interrupt and DPC load, run-queue pressure. Start at the KPI tiles, then Fleet Ranking to pick a host, then Hotspots for the shortlist.

panels.description: Hosts where this collector failed its last scrape. Non-zero means the numbers on this page are incomplete - see the Collector scrape health row at the bottom.
panels.title: Scrape FAIL

panels.description: Sustained >= 85% busy means requests are queueing. Check Fleet Ranking, then the process dashboard for the owning process.
panels.title: Hosts CPU >= 85%

panels.description: Early-warning band. Growing count over days = capacity planning trigger.
panels.title: Hosts CPU >= 70%

panels.description: Worst host right now.
panels.title: Max Busy %

panels.description: Typical host. If the median is high the whole fleet is hot, not just one server.
panels.title: Median Busy %

panels.description: Overall utilisation of the selected hosts - use for consolidation decisions.
panels.title: Fleet Avg Busy %

panels.description: High privileged time points at drivers, antivirus filters or heavy I/O rather than application code.
panels.title: Max Kernel %

panels.description: Threads waiting for a core. Queue pressure with moderate CPU% usually means too few vCPUs.
panels.title: Run Queue > 5

panels.description: Total logical processors in the current selection.
panels.title: Logical CPUs

panels.description: Pick your investigation target here.
panels.title: Top Busy % (100 - Idle)

panels.description: Kernel-heavy hosts: check storage drivers, NIC offload and security filters.
panels.title: Top Kernel (Privileged) %

panels.description: Very high interrupt rates indicate a device or virtualisation problem.
panels.title: Top Interrupts/s

panels.description: One row per host, sortable and filterable. Kernel % much larger than User % means the cost is in drivers or I/O, not the application.
panels.title: CPU Health by Host

panels.description: Watchlist. Empty table = nothing above the warning band.

targets.expr: (100 * avg by(instance) (rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",mode="privileged"}[5m]))) and on(instance) ((100 * (1 - avg by(instance) (rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",mode="idle"}[5m])))) >= 70)

panels.title: Hotspots: CPU >= 70%

panels.description: Saturated hosts. Expect user-visible latency - escalate or add vCPU.

targets.expr: (100 * avg by(instance) (rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",mode="user"}[5m]))) and on(instance) ((100 * (1 - avg by(instance) (rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"${job:regex}",instance=~"${instance:regex}",mode="idle"}[5m])))) >= 85)

panels.title: Hotspots: CPU >= 85% (act now)

panels.description: Shape matters: flat-topped at 100% = saturation, spiky = batch jobs. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: CPU Busy % (topk 10)

panels.description: Where the cycles go across the selection. A growing privileged/interrupt band is an infrastructure problem, growing user is an application problem.
panels.title: CPU Composition (fleet average)

panels.description: Compare the two bands per host to classify the load.
panels.title: Kernel vs User % (topk 10 each)

panels.description: Step changes usually follow a driver update or a NIC/HBA fault. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Interrupts/s (topk 10)

panels.description: Deferred procedure calls - high rates accompany heavy network or storage interrupt work.
panels.title: DPCs/s (topk 10)

panels.description: Sustained queue above 2 per core means the host needs more CPU.
panels.title: Run Queue Length (topk 10)

panels.description: Drops below nominal indicate thermal or power-policy throttling.
panels.title: Core Frequency MHz (topk 10)

panels.description: Effective frequency vs base frequency. Below 100% on a busy host means the power plan is limiting you.
panels.title: Processor Performance % (topk 10)

panels.description: Deep C-state residency adds wake-up latency for latency-sensitive workloads.
panels.title: C-State Residency (fleet avg by state)

panels.description: Timer interrupt rate - a proxy for how many timers applications are arming.
panels.title: Clock Interrupts/s (topk 10)

panels.description: How often cores are pulled out of idle. High values prevent power savings and add jitter.
panels.title: Idle Break Events/s (topk 10)

panels.description: FAIL rows mean every metric on this dashboard is stale for that host. Fix the exporter first, then re-read the KPIs.
panels.title: Scrape Health by Host

panels.description: Growing duration usually means the host is under load or the collector is querying more objects. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Scrape Duration (topk 10)

panels.description: Dips to 0 mark scrape gaps. Correlate with the flat spots you see in the trend panels above.
panels.title: Scrape Success (bottomk 10)
